title: A CROOKED SMILE AT CHRISTMAS
passages: It was a lonely Christmas season. I said that plainly. Emotional turbulence had pulled my attention toward creativity, healing, and purpose, but it hadn't made the loneliness disappear.

I still wanted to dress up. Still wanted to make something. Still wanted to laugh. The circus gave me a language for holding all of that at once: a costume, a crooked smile, a little smudged makeup. Joy and grief could share the same show. I didn't have to wait until I felt wonderful to make something honest.
